knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Stateful device operations leak allocator or pinned-memory state into subsequent unrelated allocations
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: API calls that change internal memory or allocator state may not restore isolation between device and host allocators, causing later tensor allocations to inherit unintended attributes such as pinned-memory status.

risk_dimensions.shape: Shape variations may affect allocation paths and state retention; include scalar, zero-dim, and high-dim tensor shapes.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Integer CUDA tensor dtypes may traverse stateful quantized-tensor construction paths with allocator side effects.
risk_dimensions.memory: Pinned-memory or allocator flags may leak across operations, especially when a CPU allocation follows a CUDA stateful operation.
risk_dimensions.device: CUDA-to-CPU transitions can reveal cross-device allocator state contamination.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Internal allocator or pinned-memory state persists across unrelated operations and changes subsequent tensor allocation behavior.

failure_mechanism.description: A stateful operation on a CUDA tensor modifies allocator or pinned-memory state that is not reset, causing subsequent CPU allocations to incorrectly inherit the modified state.

input_exploration: Vary CUDA integer tensor shapes and dtypes while keeping the operation valid.
Alternate stateful device/quantized operations with unrelated CPU tensor allocations.
Probe both scalar and high-dimensional CUDA tensor inputs before CPU allocation queries.
constraint_awareness: The operation may require valid integer types and supported device placement.
CPU allocator pinning state should be isolated from prior CUDA quantized-tensor operations.
Track allocator state or pinning flags before and after stateful operations.
oracle_strategy: Compare CPU tensor pinning state before and after the stateful device operation.
Flag unexpected CPU pinned-memory state as evidence of allocator state leakage.
Use allocator instrumentation or sanitizer checks where available.

transferability.reason: The principle of allocator or execution-state leakage across device boundaries applies to any stateful API that touches device memory and may influence later host allocations, not just the original quantized-tensor API.

llm_reasoning_guidance.important_considerations: Focus on stateful device or memory-related APIs and on whether later unrelated CPU allocations remain isolated from previous device-side side effects.
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that establish a baseline allocator/pinning state, invoke a stateful device operation, then allocate a fresh CPU tensor and compare observable state such as pinning flags against the baseline.
